name: create_stable_sort_metamorphic
description: Implement an ascending sort, graded by metamorphic relations (length/multiset/order/idempotence/permutation) over random inputs
prompts: Create sortlib.py defining a function stable_sort(items) that returns a new list containing all of `items` sorted in ascending order. It must preserve every element (including duplicates) - the result is a permutation of the input, in non-decreasing order.

test_setup_files.test_props.py:
import random
from collections import Counter
from sortlib import stable_sort


def check(x):
    r = stable_sort(list(x))
    assert len(r) == len(x), f"length changed: {len(r)} vs {len(x)} for {x!r}"
    assert Counter(r) == Counter(x), f"multiset changed for {x!r}: {r!r}"
    assert all(r[i] <= r[i + 1] for i in range(len(r) - 1)), f"not sorted: {r!r}"
    assert stable_sort(list(r)) == r, f"not idempotent for {x!r}"
    s = list(x)
    random.shuffle(s)
    assert stable_sort(s) == r, f"not permutation-invariant for {x!r}"


random.seed(1234)
for x in ([], [1], [2, 2, 2], [3, 1, 2], [5, -1, 5, 0, 5]):
    check(x)
for _ in range(300):
    n = random.randint(0, 40)
    check([random.randint(-5, 5) for _ in range(n)])
print("PASS")
